habitat: Grassland with cattle or wild grazers, especially buffalo. It seldom feeds in the water. Roosts and breeds in reeds or in trees over water, and flies to the roost morning and evening.
summary: A small, short-billed white egret of grazing herds. From October to March, breeding adults grow buff plumes on the head, back and breast. The bill is short and yellow, coral when breeding, and the legs match the bill. The feet are dusky. The immature is smaller than a Little Egret, with a shorter, thicker neck and black feet. Resident numbers rise in summer when birds arrive from central Africa.

similar.note: Little Egret is larger and more slender, with a long black bill, black legs and yellow feet, and it feeds in the shallows. Cattle Egret has a short yellow bill and walks with grazers.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^8=256 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 128–512.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the voice. The texts do not separate the sexes. The catalogue cut is not labelled by sex. Grade A from South Africa.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman says residents are joined in summer by birds from central Africa, and that buff plumes are present only from October to March, which is the southern summer, so those plumes are the breeding variant. Chick down is not described. The photograph is CC0. The call is grade A from South Africa.
